title: Rotate Array

content.problemStatement:
You're given a list of integers and a non-negative number of steps `k`.

**Rotate the list to the right by `k` positions, meaning each element moves `k` spots toward the end, wrapping around to the front when it runs off the end, and return the rotated list.**

If `k` is larger than the length of the list, treat it as if you rotated by `k` modulo the length (rotating a full lap brings you back to where you started).
constraints: k can be larger than nums.length, in which case only k mod nums.length steps actually matter
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: the last 3 elements (5,6,7) wrap around to the front, and the rest shift right by 3
the last 2 elements move to the front, pushing the first 2 to the back
rotating by 0 steps leaves the array unchanged

solution.approach: Three-step in-place reversal: 1) Reverse entire array, 2) Reverse first k elements, 3) Reverse remaining n-k elements.

bruteForce.description: Rotate the array by 1 step k times. Each 1-step rotation shifts all n elements right by 1, storing the last element at the front.

better.description: Use an extra array of length n. Place each element nums[i] at (i + k) % n in the new array, then copy back.

optimal.description: Reverse the entire array so the last k elements are at the front in reverse order. Then reverse the first k elements to restore their original order, and reverse the remaining n-k elements to restore their order.

hints: The simplest approach is using an extra array of size n, but can you rotate the array in-place using O(1) extra space?
Notice what happens if you reverse the entire array: elements move to the opposite side, but their internal order is inverted.
If you reverse the whole array [0..n-1], then reverse the first k elements [0..k-1], and finally reverse the remaining [k..n-1], every element lands in its correctly rotated spot!
learningObjectives: Understand cyclic rotation and index shifting with modular arithmetic (k % n).
Master the 3-step array reversal technique for O(1) auxiliary space in-place rotation.
Identify boundary conditions where k exceeds the array length (k >= n) or equals zero.
